module: Library for writing and reading CSV/TSV files. newCSV/newTSV create a writer (csvWriter) to which rows are added with add, then the file is written with write (timestamped name) or the text is retrieved with dump. readFileCSV and decode read a CSV (RFC 4180) back into an array of rows. Useful for recording telemetry or curves from a mod.
usage:
local csv = require('csvlib').newCSV('t', 'rpm', 'torque')
csv:add(0.0, 800, 120)
csv:add(0.1, 900, 130)
local name = csv:write('mylog')  -- mylog_2026-...csv
local rows = require('csvlib').readFileCSV(name)
notes: The file requires 'utils'; write uses writeFile (global) and readFileCSV uses readFile (global).
Numbers are written in %.10g format; booleans are 1/0; nil gives an empty cell; strings are quoted if necessary (separator, quote, CR, LF, or starts with a space/control character).
The default file name comes from the first letters of the headers (headernym), otherwise 'csv' or 'tsv'.
write appends _YYYY-MM-DDTHH_MM_SS.ext unless the 4th character from the end of the name is a dot (name already has a 3-letter extension).
decode converts to number the unquoted fields that start with a digit, + or - when tonumber succeeds; ignores spaces/tabs around values; removes trailing empty cells and trailing empty lines.
Quoted cells remain strings, even if they look like a number.
The headernym field is only defined if headers are passed to newCSV/newTSV, and only the first letter is kept (underscore for an empty header); add(...) with the headers writes the first row.

newCSV.desc: Creates a CSV writer (comma separator). Any arguments form the header row.

newTSV.desc: Creates a TSV writer (tab separator). Any arguments form the header row.

readFileCSV.desc: Reads a file via readFile then decodes it with decode.

returns.desc: Array of rows, each row being an array of values; nil if the file is unreadable.

decode.desc: Decodes CSV text (RFC 4180) into an array of rows of cells.

returns.desc: Rows of cells (numbers or strings); nil if s is nil.

csvWriter.desc: Object returned by newCSV/newTSV. Accumulates the text in a string.buffer.

add.desc: Adds a row of cells (numbers, booleans, strings or nil).

dump.desc: Returns all the accumulated content as text.

write.desc: Writes the content to a file (see notes for naming).

filename.desc: Name or path; by default derived from the headers.
